papers.title: Long-lived light-driven bimagnons at finite momentum in NiO
papers.abstract: Light can manipulate magnetic order and its excitations on ultrafast timescales, including through resonantly driven phonons. In antiferromagnets, light can also create correlated magnon pairs, or bimagnons. Unlike single magnons, whose damping has been measured and modeled in detail, little is known about the lifetime, interactions and decay of such correlated pairs: prior two-magnon measurements show broad linewidths or coherences that dephase within 200 fs. Here we pump the phonon-assisted two-magnon absorption of NiO with mid-infrared pulses, far below its bandgap, and probe the resulting magnetic dynamics at finite momentum with time-resolved resonant inelastic X-ray scattering (RIXS). Upon photoexcitation, the one-magnon linewidth and energy are essentially unchanged, indicating that the long-range magnetic order is preserved without the photocarrier-induced demagnetization characteristic of above-bandgap excitation. A pump-induced two-magnon signal appears on the energy-gain (anti-Stokes) side of the spectrum. Its spectral weight peaks 4 ps after the pump, well beyond our 0.5 ps time resolution, indicative of a delayed growth likely due to momentum redistribution of the light-induced magnon pairs across the Brillouin zone. This two-magnon signal decays with a time constant of $28\pm11$ ps, exceeding the previously reported two-magnon dephasing time by more than two orders of magnitude. These results establish long-lived light-driven bimagnon correlations beyond the one-magnon state, akin to the higher-order correlations measured in ultracold gases.

papers.title: Discrete Time Crystals from Anti-Unitary Floquet Driving and Dynamical Freezing
papers.abstract: We show anti-unitary periodic drive paves a direct path for stabilizing a Discrete Time-Crystal by Dynamical Freezing (DF). The magnetization appears as an emergent conserved operator, and an exact pairing of two-cycle quasi-energies pins the subharmonic response. DF keeps the effective Hamiltonian $\textit{quasi-local}$; infinite-chain simulations show no detectable decay for a generic state with any finite magnetization. We outline an experimental realization of the anti-unitary drive.

papers.title: Ensemble phase transitions in measurement-unitary hybrid quantum circuits
papers.abstract: The universal properties of state ensembles generated by quantum dynamics provide a refined lens into Hilbert-space ergodicity and deep thermalisation, or lack thereof. We investigate deep-ergodicity breaking transitions of an ancillary qubit entangled with a system undergoing dynamics via hybrid quantum circuits, where unitary evolution is interspersed with projective measurements. Specifically, we analyse the statistical properties of two distinct state ensembles: the trajectory ensemble (TE) conditioned on the measurement outcomes of the hybrid circuit, and the projected ensemble (PE) generated by further projective measurements of the system at the final temporal boundary. We find that both ensembles undergo non-analytic changes -- ensemble phase transitions -- at the critical point of the measurement-induced purification transition, despite their first moments remaining completely maximally mixed and blind to the transition. For Haar-random circuits, the TE transitions from a trivial identity ensemble to the uniform Haar ensemble, while the PE transitions from the Haar ensemble to a trivial singleton pure state. In Clifford circuits, absence of non-stabiliserness limits the PE to a $1$-design, while the TE forms a $k$-design for $k \leq 3$. We demonstrate that these genuine ensemble transitions offer a clear physical mechanism for the measurement-induced entanglement or purification transitions, illustrating how the capacity to ergodically steer a quantum subsystem shifts from the temporal boundary measurements in the mixed phase to the bulk trajectory measurements in the pure phase.

papers.title: Quantum Metrology and Quantum Battery in a Hyperfine-Coupled Spin System
papers.abstract: We investigate multiparameter quantum metrology and the energetic properties of an effective electron--proton spin system inspired by the hyperfine structure of the hydrogen atom. Considering the external magnetic field $\mathcal B$ and the hyperfine coupling strength $Λ$ as unknown parameters, we derive the quantum Fisher information matrix and establish the corresponding quantum Cramér--Rao bounds for their simultaneous estimation. We analyze the estimation precision and the correlations between the two parameters, showing that the weak-commutativity condition is satisfied despite the noncommutativity of the associated symmetric logarithmic derivatives. Independently, we explore the energetic properties of the system under a unitary charging protocol, characterizing its ergotropy, anti-ergotropy, storage capacity, and energy-basis coherence. We investigate the dependence of these quantities on the magnetic field, hyperfine coupling, temperature, and charging time. Our results provide a comprehensive characterization of the metrological properties and energetic performance of a hyperfine spin-based quantum system, highlighting its potential as a platform for quantum sensing and energy storage.

papers.title: Statistics of Fock-space correlation lengths in the many-body localised phase
papers.abstract: The presence of long-ranged, many-body resonances in the many-body localised phase of disordered quantum systems is manifest in strong inhomogeneities of eigenstate amplitudes on the Fock space. We develop a quantitative, microscopic theory for this, centred on two-point Fock-space correlation functions. Exact diagonalisation of the disordered tilted-field Ising chain uncovers a stark contrast: typical correlations decay perfectly exponentially, whereas average correlations exhibit subexponential decay with systematic system-size dependence driven by rare resonant nodes. We show that this behaviour stems from an underlying distribution of Fock-space correlation lengths with a variance that scales inversely with system size. Crucially, the interplay of this distribution with the high-dimensional geometry of the hypercubic Fock-space graph, leads to the qualitative difference between the typical and average behaviours. The theory also allows us to derive the singularity spectrum of the many-body localised eigenstates, and to establish theoretically the anomalous symmetry violation of quantum multifractality as an inherent consequence of the Fock-space geometry.

papers.title: Traces of Vacuum Squeezing: A Superconducting Transmission-Line Analogue of Cosmological Particle Creation
papers.abstract: Particle creation in time-dependent quantum fields is a central phenomenon in early-universe cosmology, yet it remains experimentally inaccessible in its original context. We show theoretically that superconducting circuits based on a waveguide-like transmission line loaded with dc-SQUIDs can provide a direct analogue of a scalar field in a radiation-dominated Friedmann--Robertson--Walker universe in conformal time. The mode equation of the circuit reduces to the Weber equation, the same equation governing cosmological particle creation in a radiation-dominated background, admitting an exact solution in terms of parabolic cylinder functions and an exponentially suppressed particle spectrum. We analyse the conditions under which the analogy holds, which require a compromise between the duration of the pulse, the uniformity of the modulation and the symmetry of the SQUIDs, and show that dissipation does not erase the cosmological signal. We use the anomalous moment of each mode as a witness of the Bogoliubov mixing: it vanishes for any thermal state and survives dissipation, and, together with the photon number, it certifies squeezing, and with the purity of the state, it identifies whether the pairs created from the vacuum dominate.

papers.title: Sharp Uniform Fisher Information Bounds from Projective Designs
papers.abstract: Fixed measurements for multiparameter pure-state metrology must remain informative without knowing the input state. We quantify this requirement by the Fisher floor, the smallest fraction of the quantum Fisher information that a measurement retains over all pure states and tangent directions. We determine the Fisher guarantees, namely lower bounds on Fisher floors, implied by projective design order alone in every dimension $d\ge 2$. These guarantees are sharp at order $t=2$ and every odd order $t\ge 3$, and finite weighted designs attain them; at even orders, our bounds are nearly tight. As the order increases, the guarantees approach one half, the single-copy quantum limit. Sampling and spectral completion of any 3-design yield, with probability $1-O(1/d)$, a measurement with linearly many outcomes and a dimension-independent Fisher floor. Such a measurement separates all pure states in Hellinger distance, so pure-state maximum-likelihood estimation from $N$ copies attains mean infidelity $O(d/N)$ uniformly over pure states, optimal up to a universal constant factor.

papers.title: Near-Optimal Multiparameter Pure-State Metrology with a Constant Number of Bases
papers.abstract: Multiparameter pure-state metrology is limited by the incompatibility of measurements optimized for different parameters. We characterize uniform sensitivity by the Fisher floor, the smallest fraction of the quantum Fisher information (QFI) retained over all pure states and parameter directions. We prove that a constant number of fixed orthonormal bases suffices for a nearly optimal Fisher floor, independently of the Hilbert-space dimension $d$. With high probability, five independent Haar bases already achieve a positive, dimension-independent floor, and larger constant families achieve approximate universal Fisher symmetry: they retain nearly one half of the QFI in every direction, the largest uniform fraction permitted by measurement incompatibility. The required number of bases is optimal up to a logarithmic factor in inverse accuracy. In contrast, $d+1$ mutually unbiased bases, when they exist, can minimize mean Fisher anisotropy among families of $d+1$ bases yet have a Fisher floor of at most $1/(d+1)$, showing that optimal average balance does not ensure uniform sensitivity.

papers.title: Stiffness in Confined Quantum Walks
papers.abstract: We investigate boundary-induced stiffness in discrete-time quantum walks confined to a finite lattice by unitary reflecting boundaries implemented through coin-flip operations. We define a dimensionless spreading stiffness from the instantaneous variation of the spatial width relative to the asymptotic spreading rate of the corresponding unconfined Hadamard walk and compare localized, Gaussian, and truncated-uniform initial states. The long-time response retains a strong dependence on the initial spatial profile: the localized and truncated-uniform states show an overall increase in stiffness with increasing confinement size, whereas the Gaussian state exhibits a nonmonotonic dependence with a broad maximum at intermediate sizes. The first and second stiffness moments satisfy the expected asymptotic consistency relation in the high-stiffness regime. The normalized Kullback--Leibler divergence reveals a slower spatial reorganization and qualitatively different finite-size trends, showing that dynamical stiffness and spatial homogenization are distinct properties. These results indicate that unitary confinement produces an intrinsically nonstationary regime whose long-time properties emerge from the interplay between boundary reflections, system size, and the spatial structure of the initial state.

papers.title: Observation of Genuine Multi-Time Quantum Memory
papers.abstract: Memory effects in open quantum systems do not by themselves imply quantum memory, since non-Markovian dynamics can often be reproduced by classical-memory models. Known criteria certify the presence of quantum memory in the environment by comparing the evolution of the system at two different times. We show that quantum memory can remain hidden from all such pairwise tests and become detectable only when three or more times are considered jointly. We derive an analytical three-time witness and use it to certify quantum memory in a minimal qubit example in which every pair of times has a classical-memory explanation, thus establishing a strict hierarchy of quantum memory effects. Genuine multi-time quantum memory does not rely on fine-tuned time-dependent Hamiltonians or gate-based evolution. We experimentally demonstrate the hierarchy of quantum memory in a time-continuous realization on a superconducting-qubit platform with time-independent couplings.

papers.title: A deployed four-city entanglement-based QKD network with real-time key delivery, benchmarked against finite-key security bounds
papers.abstract: Quantum key distribution (QKD) generates shared secret keys whose security rests on the laws of physics rather than on computational assumptions. We report the entanglement-based segment of the Slovak national quantum communication infrastructure, connecting four cities in western Slovakia over deployed telecommunication fiber. Polarization-entangled photons generated at a central node are passively routed by wavelength to form a trusted-node-free, fully meshed sub-network of three cities, with the fourth connected through the central node and all links operated simultaneously. We also introduce a matrix formalism for passive wavelength routing that enables the algorithmic construction of uniquely and fully connected topologies. Unlike most previous demonstrations, which estimate key rates from raw coincidences, all rates reported here are obtained after the complete post-processing chain, with keys delivered in real time via ETSI GS QKD 014. With partial non-local chromatic dispersion compensation, we obtain 13.5 bit/s over 109 km, and 4.3 bit/s over 32.1 dB of accumulated loss between two cities without a direct fiber link. Benchmarking against finite-key security bounds shows that the implemented heuristic privacy amplification can exceed the finite-key bound, and that replacing detect-and-discard with error correction would increase the finite-key rate by a factor of 4.1-6.6, and yield a positive finite-key rate on the 142.9 km link where the implemented scheme yields none.

papers.title: Scalable Pauli propagation through $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear partitioning
papers.abstract: Pauli propagation simulates quantum circuits and many-body dynamics by evolving observables in the Heisenberg picture as sparse sums of Pauli strings. As Pauli-string operations reduce to bit manipulations, its performance is limited by memory bandwidth and capacity rather than computational throughput. Pooling the memory of many cores and nodes is hindered by the deduplication step after every gate, which can require global synchronization. We avoid this bottleneck by partitioning the strings with an $\mathbb{F}_2$-linear hash function, which guarantees that a $k$-qubit channel couples each partition to at most $4^k$ partitions fixed by the gate, decomposing gate application into independent tasks with bounded communication. Benchmarks of our open-source implementation demonstrate efficient parallel scaling within and across compute nodes, enabling simulations with over $10^{11}$ Pauli strings and extending the accessible timescales of quantum many-body dynamics.

papers.title: Non-interferometric tests of gravitational decoherence models with mechanical oscillators
papers.abstract: Phenomenological models of quantum-gravity-induced decoherence can leave observable effects even in experiments that do not rely on interferometric measurements. We study three such models, based respectively on deformed relativistic symmetries, stochastic metric fluctuations, and a stochastic generalized uncertainty principle, all of which induce decoherence in the momentum basis. For a free particle, the models preserve momentum distribution and mean energy but produce position diffusion and momentum-space decoherence with model-specific momentum dependences. For a harmonic oscillator, the noncommutativity of the collapse operators with the oscillator Hamiltonian results in anomalous heating, with the three models leading to qualitatively different energy dynamics. The first gives heating at a constant rate, the second at a rate proportional to the kinetic energy, which can lead to exponential growth, and the third at a rate growing cubically with excitation. We further derive the stationary position power spectral density and show that all three models produce the same leading-order excess lineshape in the weak-noise regime, distinct from that of force noise. Comparing with existing mechanical platforms, we find that displacement-noise measurements can already constrain the fluctuation time of the first model below the Planck time, while occupation measurements could improve the bounds on the second model by up to fourteen orders of magnitude over those from ground-state heating of levitated particles. Summing the heating over all phonon modes of a solid, the residual heat release of low-temperature experiments constrains the first model far below the Planck time and the second at the Planck time. Our results establish heating and continuous measurements as complementary non-interferometric probes of gravity-related decoherence.

papers.title: Implementation of a 1D Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD under finite-size parameter estimation
papers.abstract: Continuous-variable quantum key distribution (CV-QKD) is a promising technology for quantum-secure communications, offering high secret-key rates and straightforward integration with coherent optical communication systems. Conventional Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD encodes information in both optical-field quadratures, increasing requirements for state preparation, modulation, and calibration, while potentially introducing additional preparation imperfections. Unidimensional (1D) Gaussian modulation offers a simpler alternative by encoding information in only one quadrature, while the conjugate quadrature constrains the protocol's security. However, an integrated experimental 1D implementation combining independent-laser coherent reception with practical reconciliation, finite-size parameter estimation, and privacy amplification remains challenging. Here, we experimentally demonstrate a 1D Gaussian-modulated CV-QKD system over 12~km of standard single-mode fiber using a local local oscillator (LLO) architecture with independent lasers and an integrated offline classical post-processing chain. The implementation includes coherent detection, digital signal processing, information reconciliation, parameter estimation, physicality-constrained security analysis, and privacy amplification. The 1D system achieves a privacy-amplified rate of $1.421$~Mbit/s under the asymptotic security treatment and $0.364$~Mbit/s under the finite-size scenario. These results establish an experimental baseline for the performance--complexity trade-off associated with unidimensional Gaussian modulation and provide an experimental basis for developing lower-complexity CV-QKD transmitters.

papers.title: Programming Quantum Circuit Parameters with Large Language Models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) have recently demonstrated the ability to generate parameters for variational quantum circuits without conventional optimization. However, the conditions under which this approach is effective remain unclear. Here, we investigate a frozen, general-purpose LLM that generates complete circuit parameter vectors from symbolic circuit and Hamiltonian descriptions, with optional iterative energy feedback. We evaluate the approach on general random Hamiltonians, structured parent Hamiltonians, and molecular systems. For general Hamiltonians, LLM-generated parameters exhibit larger energy errors than conventional Adam optimization, while additional feedback generally provides limited improvement. In contrast, for structured Hamiltonians, the LLM can generate promising low-energy parameter configurations, suggesting that identifiable physical and mathematical structure facilitates parameter inference. We also show that direct LLM predictions of minimum energies can violate the Hamiltonian spectral lower bound, whereas generated circuit parameters allow independent evaluation of physically realizable energy expectation values. Finally, we investigate blind circuit interpretation and find that the LLM can predict measurement outcomes even when it fails to identify the underlying quantum algorithm. These findings highlight the role of problem structure, the limitations of iterative LLM optimization, and the importance of independently verifiable predictions in quantum parameter programming.

papers.title: Quantum Boltzmann Equation for Static Correlation with Cumulant Kernel Closure
papers.abstract: We present a Quantum Boltzmann Equation for static correlation by mapping the Bogoliubov-Born-Green-Kirkwood-Yvon hierarchy to discrete atomic-orbital matrix mechanics via the Wigner-Weyl isomorphism to evaluate scattering of the correlated two-body cumulant. This Quantum Boltzmann Equation converges to the active-space static correlation limit and preserves pure $N$-representability constraints during the kinetic relaxation. To resolve scaling bottlenecks of explicit two-body cumulant methods, we project the two-body cumulant onto its lowest unitary invariant and evaluate a susceptibility-windowed orbital scattering scale via a single Coulomb-exchange contraction. Relaxing onto a hyperbolic-tangent cumulant attractor through Markovian collisional relaxation yields a parameter-free Quantum Boltzmann Equation Cumulant-Kernel that regularizes derivative cusps without thermal smearing. Using the collinear $\mathrm{H}_3$ exchange reaction, the symmetric $D_{4h}$ square $\mathrm{H}_4$ dissociation, the non-adiabatic avoided crossing in $\mathrm{BeH}_2$, the symmetric bond cleavage of $\mathrm{H}_2\mathrm{O}$, the triple-bond dissociation of $\mathrm{N}_2$, the 11-molecule MR-MGN-BE17 dissociation test set, and the singlet diradical isomers of benzyne as case studies, we show that this kinetic relaxation resolves strong static correlation at zero electronic temperature.

papers.title: Explicit Absolutely Maximally Entangled states in dimensions twice a prime power
papers.abstract: Absolutely maximally entangled (AME) states are pure multipartite states with maximally mixed reductions on every set of at most half the parties. We construct explicit families in local dimension $2q$, twice an odd prime power $q$, using an established coupling of qubits and $q$-level systems. The $q$-level states remove interference between branches, so the qubit states need maximally mixed reductions only on average. This gives AME$(9,2q)$ and AME$(11,2q)$ for every odd prime power $q\geq5$, AME$(13,2q)$ for $q\geq17$, AME$(15,2q)$ for $q\geq9$, and AME$(17,2q)$ for $q\geq67$. For every odd $N\geq3$, the same coupling gives AME$(N,2q)$ under the sufficient condition $q\geq\max\{N,2^{N-2}\}$ on the odd prime power $q$. Within this coupling, the smallest such $q$ must grow exponentially with $N$. Combined with known inputs and products, these families complete the nine-party classification: for integer $d\geq2$, an AME$(9,d)$ state exists if and only if $d\geq3$. Choosing the branch pairing also gives AME$(15,2p)$ states with a cyclic shift of the parties compensated by local unitaries, for every prime $p\equiv1\pmod{15}$.

papers.title: Lattice response theory for subsystem symmetry-protected topological phases
papers.abstract: We develop a framework to study subsystem symmetry-protected topological (SSPT) phases using lattice response theory. We begin with a systematic construction of spacetime lattice gauge fields from general microscopic $X$-type symmetry actions on qudit systems, including global symmetries, subsystem symmetries, and more general modulated symmetries. Given a gauge-invariant response action, we then construct a corresponding entangler and explicitly show that it implements stacking with the SSPT phase described by the response action. We show that a broad class of SSPT phases can be described by intersection pairings and realized by cluster entanglers. We also study SSPT phases beyond intersection pairings, including those described by subsystem analogues of type-II group cocycles involving the Bockstein homomorphism. We construct a new 3+1d SSPT phase protected by two 2-foliated planar subsystem symmetries and a global 0-form symmetry, whose response action is a subsystem analogue of a type-III cocycle. On its boundary, the 0-form symmetry acts by stacking with a 2+1d linear SSPT phase, signaling a mixed 't Hooft anomaly.

papers.title: Efficient computation of PEPS gradients for optimized quantum state preparation on 2D topologies
papers.abstract: Quantum state preparation is a fundamental subroutine for quantum computation. For complex, entangled initial states it is, however, difficult to prepare shallow quantum circuits approximating the state with sufficient accuracy. Tensor networks provide a promising avenue of synthesis of such circuits, but most approaches employ 1D Matrix Products States, which struggle to accurately express entangled states in higher dimensions. Here we present a hardware topology-aware quantum state preparation method based on gradient optimization of 2D projected entangled pair states (PEPS). Our approach combines local disentanglement, with global fine tuning based on PEPS gradient optimization. Towards this end we describe an efficient procedure for PEPS gradient computation. We test the convergence and performance of our method in numerical simulations.

papers.title: Generalized ladder operators and construction of families of superintegrable systems with Painlevé VI
papers.abstract: We study quantum Hamiltonians whose separated angular component is expressed through a generic Painlevé VI transcendent. We construct generalized ladder operators for one-dimensional Schrödinger operators with a quadratic spectral variable. For the Painlevé VI angular Hamiltonian these operators satisfy $[N,J_\pm]=\pm2kJ_\pm$, where $N=\sqrt M$, and close through an eighth-degree norm polynomial. Combining the angular shifts with the radial shift operators of the oscillator, Coulomb and free Bessel systems yields higher-order integrals and deformed Racah-type polynomial algebras for the two-dimensional superintegrable models. This construction provides new families of Tremblay-Turbiner-Winternitz (TTW)- and Post-Winternitz (PW)-like Hamiltonians with integrals of arbitrarily high order and Painlevé VI in the potential. This framework also recovers models from the classification of third- and fourth-order integrals as particular cases. For a representative oscillator extension we compute the Casimir explicitly and recover the finite-dimensional energy spectrum from a deformed-oscillator realization. We then analyze the special-solution sector using the explicit families collected by Gromak, Laine and Shimomura. The resulting potentials are organized into a small number of spectral classes, and the distinction between formal zeros of the ladder norm and physical self-adjoint representations is made explicit. The regular nonclassical rational examples are rational Darboux deformations of the trigonometric Pöschl--Teller system and lead to strictly isospectral exceptional-Jacobi sectors or to state-adding representations with an isolated angular level. A singular branch produces an interior inverse-square barrier and a split-domain problem. For one regular exceptional sector and two state-adding sectors we display the polynomial algebras.

papers.title: Multi-particle quantum walk search on a two-dimensional lattice
papers.abstract: In the present paper we study the formulation of a search problem and the efficiency of multi-particle quantum walk search algorithms. The discrete-time evolution of each particle in space is treated according to Grover's quantum walk evolution operator. We focus on the local interactions models, where the particles' states are modified only when two or more of them appear on the same grid site. The main focus is given to the two-dimensional grid in space. We study the dependence of the search algorithm asymptotic success time and probability on the interaction strength and the generated maximal entanglement between particles. We show that the interacting and non-interacting two- and three-particle search algorithm attains a constant factor improvement over the single-particle counterpart. In addition, we provide a new generalized model of interactions for multi-particle quantum walks.

papers.title: Gaussian ergotropy and spatial correlations: accelerated vacuum versus a thermal field
papers.abstract: Can the spatial correlations of a quantum environment be revealed through work extraction? We address this question using two harmonic-oscillator detectors coupled to either an accelerated vacuum or a matched inertial thermal field. We establish a quantitative connection between the spatial correlations of the environment and the equilibrium Gaussian ergotropy, showing that the leading extractable work is governed by a response-weighted spatial correlation. Although the two environments have identical local spectra, their different spatial correlations give rise to distinct work responses. We further identify a finite-distance blind point at which a single measurement configuration fails to distinguish the two environments. By reversing the direct coupling between the detectors, we develop a two-setting scheme that removes this ambiguity and reconstructs the underlying spatial correlations from work measurements. This reconstruction remains effective beyond the weak-coupling regime. We also show that spatial correlations can provide additional global work even when the detector pair is separable, demonstrating that entanglement is not a necessary resource for this advantage. Finally, we investigate the transient evolution of Gaussian ergotropy and reveal its oscillatory decay and dependence on acceleration and detector parameters. Our results establish Gaussian ergotropy as an operational probe of spatial correlations in bosonic environments.

papers.title: Noise robust super-Heisenberg scaling in time-dependent quantum sensing by subspace-twirled dynamical decoupling
papers.abstract: In quantum parameter estimation, time-dependent Hamiltonians can enable ultraprecise estimates of a physical parameter beyond the standard Heisenberg limit, also called the super-Heisenberg limit. However, achieving optimal scaling of the measurement precision typically requires an adaptive quantum control scheme which is resource-intensive and hard to implement in general. Furthermore, this advantage is often severely eroded by environmental noise. We propose the use of a dynamical decoupling scheme based on subspace twirling -- the averaging of random unitaries over a subspace rather than the entire Hilbert space -- to overcome these two limitations. We first prove necessary and sufficient conditions for subspace twirling to preserve the encoding signal while simultaneously removing environmental noise. We then establish conditions and provide performance guarantees for when time dependent Hamiltonians undergoing subspace twirling can achieve super-Heisenberg scaling without adaptive controls. Finally, we illustrate our results using an explicit example where a qubit sensor undergoing a subspace twirl simultaneously suppresses noise and achieves super-Heisenberg scaling. These results offer guidance for the design of ultraprecise quantum sensors under time-dependent and noisy conditions.

papers.title: Physical Observables and Superselection
papers.abstract: It is well-known that a physical state may be represented by a unit vector in a Hilbert space, whilst a physical observable may be represented by a self-adjoint operator on that same space. However, the introduction of a superselection rule on a Hilbert space imposes constraints such that not all self-adjoint operators can represent observables, which has further consequences for the states themselves as well as the physical processes that transform them. In this article, we review the concept of superselection from the view of how such rules would affect what we consider to be physical. Arguments for the existence of a superselection rule due to charge or possibly energy conservation are given and the emergence of effective superselection rules due to decoherence or the lack of a shared reference frame are also discussed.

papers.title: Ergodicity breaking for data classification in a dissipative Ising model with competing two- and four-body interactions
papers.abstract: We explore the close relationship between the processing of data and the dynamics of interacting many-body systems. For example, certain classes of quantum neural networks can be mapped onto dissipative quantum Ising models whose evolution is described by a Lindblad master equation. In these architectures, emergent nonlinearities lead to non-ergodic dynamics under which initial states located in different basins of attraction evolve towards distinguishable stationary states. This mechanism underlies the classification of quantum data. Motivated by this connection, we consider an Ising model with competing two- and four-body interactions. Using a combination of mean-field calculations and exact small-scale numerics, we show that the stationary state manifold can be designed to enable multi-class classification. We also investigate the structure of the ensuing basins of attraction, thereby showing that these systems allow for the classification of quantum states with nonlinear decision boundaries.

papers.title: Entanglement detection from moments of the realigned state: application to continuous-variable quantum systems
papers.abstract: Certifying entanglement is a central problem in quantum information sciences, especially for continuous-variable quantum systems where full state tomography is experimentally demanding. We introduce a family of separability criteria based on the singular moments and weak moments of the operator obtained by applying the realignment map to the density operator. In practice, we find that the criterion based on the second-order moments of the realigned operator is already sufficient to witness the entanglement of a wide range of quantum optical states. The realigned moments can be readily accessed using an optical scheme consisting of a linear interferometer that couples several identical copies of the state, similarly to the multicopy technique used to measure the partial-transpose moments of a state [Phys. Rev. Research 8, 033064 (2026)]. We illustrate the detection capability of the second-order realigned-moment method for both Gaussian and non-Gaussian states, including lossy NOON states.

papers.title: Improved Low-Cost Quantum Error Mitigation with Benchmarked-Noise Zero-Noise Extrapolation (bnZNE)
papers.abstract: We theoretically extend and experimentally demonstrate benchmarked-noise zero-noise extrapolation (bnZNE), a simple and low-cost method for quantum error mitigation which aims to outperform the highly popular ZNE method for an equal total shot cost by improving the classical extrapolation step. We recently proposed bnZNE as a new error mitigation method (Harris et al., arXiv:2603.10224 (2026)) and showed that it can mitigate noise to the same order as standard ZNE under gate-wise depolarizing noise. Here, we introduce randomized bnZNE which addresses the case of running multiple random circuits per noise level, allowing for the incorporation of noise-tailoring techniques like Pauli twirling and readout error mitigation, and test the method on the IBM and IQM hardware for a plethora of large-scale applications, observing bnZNE to consistently produce more accurate results than standard ZNE. Our approach enhances the extrapolation process to the zero-noise limit by using classically-simulable and structure-mirroring benchmark circuits, generated from the standard application circuit, to sensitively measure the effective error rate at each scaled noise level beyond simple integer values. We give a new method for generating tailored benchmark circuits for the IQM superconducting devices and test them experimentally. Our results demonstrate that bnZNE presents a versatile alternative to ZNE which can enable more accurate results at utility scales with an equivalent cost.

papers.title: Lorentz Boosts and Governing Equations of the Quantum Geometric Tensor in 4D Energy-Momentum Space
papers.abstract: In solids, the quantum geometric tensor (QGT), $Q_{μν}=g_{μν}-\frac{i}{2} Ω_{μν}$, combines the quantum metric and Berry curvature. Its imaginary part governs anomalous velocity and quantized Hall transport, while its real part determines the quantum weight and geometric contributions to flat-band superfluid stiffness and dielectric response. Here, we extend the QGT to four-dimensional (4D) energy-momentum space ($ω/c,k$), treating frequency and momentum as independent coordinates. Invariance of the real-spacetime plane-wave phase fixes their Lorentz transformation in energy-momentum space. Lorentz boosts of static Dirac and Weyl systems then generate frequency metrics, quadrupolar frequency-momentum shear metrics, and electric-like Berry-Maxwell fields. We identify five Lorentz-invariant contractions and derive the governing field equations and flow conservation laws for both the quantum metric and Berry curvature from static Weyl geometry and Lorentz covariance. We further connect Gaussian spectral amplitudes of the QGT to localized Gaussian events in 4D spacetime. Finally, we discuss experimental realizations in spacetime crystals or time-varying media and clarify how this unified quantum geometry of a gravitational-like metric and electromagnetic-like gauge fields connects geometric self-consistency with physical event dynamics.

papers.title: Higher-Group Statistics on Lattices
papers.abstract: Crossing a domain wall can permute anyons, and intersecting strings can create a particle. These couplings between defects of various dimensions are specified by higher groups. We develop a lattice framework defining higher-group statistics as Berry phases of closed sequences of hopping operators, invariant under local modifications of the operators. Our central example is a closed Majorana chain, a 1-dimensional topological superconductor, embedded in 3 dimensions. We construct a loop-flip process with phase $+i$, refining the usual $\pm 1$ loop-flip invariant through intermediate transfer of fermion parity between the chain and physical fermions. In two dimensions, charge-wall statistics distinguish two $\mathbb Z_4$ toric codes enriched by $\mathbb Z_2$ charge-conjugation symmetry, with identical anyon statistics but distinct gauged theories: the quantum doubles of the dihedral group $D_4$ and the quaternion group $Q_8$. We provide two complementary constructions of statistical processes. The first extends the Smith normal form algorithm in [Phys. Rev. X $\textbf{16}$, 011010 (2026), arXiv:2412.01886] to higher groups, generating processes from lattice geometry and prescribed local moves. For a finite higher group $\mathbb G$, we prove that statistical processes on a $d$-sphere are classified by $H_{d+2}(B\mathbb G,\mathbb Z)$. The second constructs processes directly from homology classes without examining exponentially many defect configurations, enabling us to study statistics for complex higher-group structures where the previous method is computationally prohibitive. These processes detect boundary anomalies of higher-group symmetry-protected topological phases. For example, we distinguish 2-group anomalies in 1, 2, and 3 dimensions. Higher-group statistics provide new invariants for characterizing coupled defects in quantum many-body systems.

papers.title: Unified master equation for driven multilevel quantum systems: Derivation, dynamics, and spectral signatures
papers.abstract: Drive-modified dissipation in multilevel quantum systems is not, in general, accurately captured by conventional master equations. We derive a unified master equation using Lewis-Riesenfeld dynamical invariants, accommodating arbitrary driving within Born-Markov theory. We demonstrate the applicability of the unified master equation to constant-Rabi-coupling (continuous-wave), periodically-modulated-Rabi-coupling, and nonperiodic (ramped and chirped) driving protocols. Fluorescence spectra of a periodically driven three-level $Λ$ system reveal signatures missed by conventional descriptions. We trace the limitations of the conventional descriptions to inaccurate bath-frequency sampling and the neglect of nonsecular dissipative couplings, and map out the parameter regimes that require a unified treatment. The fluorescence spectra provide experimentally accessible signatures, which serve as a spectroscopic guide to reliable modeling of dissipative processes that can inform quantum control, simulation, sensing, and information processing.

papers.title: Classical Verification of Quantum Advantage via Clifford Obfuscation
papers.abstract: Demonstrating quantum advantage in a manner that can be independently verified by classical means remains one of the most pressing open problems in quantum computing. Here we propose a new heuristic approach for constructing quantum circuits that are hard to classically simulate yet whose output distributions can be efficiently verified classically. Our approach is based on Clifford circuit obfuscation. This obfuscation scheme hides the Clifford structure and injects a controlled and rapidly growing non-stabilizer resources that resist known classical attack strategies including reverse engineering and direct simulation. Our protocol is heuristic but is supported by both numerical and theoretical evidence. This work provides a new avenue toward classically verifiable quantum advantage that avoids the stringent implementation requirements of known approaches.

papers.title: ChainForge: Characterizing Embedding as the Bottleneck in Quantum Annealer Workloads
papers.abstract: Quantum Annealers (QAs) are among the first commercially scaled quantum computing systems designed for large-scale optimization. Unlike digital systems that execute sequences of compiled instructions, QAs operate as analog single-instruction machines that directly evolve an Ising Hamiltonian toward low-energy solutions. To execute an application, the logical problem graph must first be mapped onto the hardware's sparse connectivity via embedding, where logical variables are represented by chains of connected physical qubits. As a result, embedding becomes the dominant system challenge in QAs, shaping whether and how workloads can execute on the machine. Despite its central role, embedding has largely been treated as a preprocessing step rather than a system bottleneck. In this work, we present ChainForge, the first systems and architecture characterization of embedding in QA workloads. Using diverse workload families and graph topologies on modern QA hardware, we characterize how embedding impacts effective hardware capacity, routing overheads, runtime variability, and solution quality. Our results show that embedding inflates physical resource usage, long chains degrade annealing fidelity and scalability, and heuristic embedders may fail even when valid embeddings exist. We further show that embedding latency can become a runtime bottleneck for dynamic workloads requiring frequent remapping, while nominal qubit counts significantly overestimate the usable capacity of QAs for realistic applications. Overall, our findings establish embedding as the defining workload bottleneck and systems abstraction of QAs, providing architectural insights for future hardware topologies, runtime systems, and workload-aware annealing platforms.

papers.title: On the Reachability Problem in Quantum Petri Nets
papers.abstract: In this paper, we propose a novel quantum solution to address the problem of reachability in bounded quantum Petri nets (QPNs), an advanced modeling framework that combines the classical Petri net model with quantum mechanical principles. The proposed approach exploits quantum parallelism to construct a superposition over all reachable markings from the initial marking. Grover's amplitude amplification algorithm is then applied to efficiently identify a desired target marking, while ancillary q-tokens used solely for transition control are excluded from the search space, significantly reducing its size. Theoretical analysis shows that our approach achieves a quadratic speed up over classical exhaustive algorithms. Experimental results also confirm the correctness and feasibility of the proposed quantum algorithm for solving the bounded reachability problem in Quantum Petri Nets.

papers.title: Monolithic high density integrated photonics on bulk lithium niobate
papers.abstract: Functional electro-optic (EO) tunable photonic integrated circuits are crucial to next-generation information processing and advanced computing, where ferroelectric materials such as lithium niobate (LiNbO3) provide outstanding optical properties and versatile tuning mechanisms. However, beyond achieving high-performance devices, practical deployment of LiNbO3 photonic integrated circuits requires rapid and cost-effective scale-up, which remains challenging because of the fabrication complexity and high costs of ion-sliced thin-film lithium niobate and wafer bonding processes. To address this gap, we demonstrate a fully monolithic photonic platform, amorphous silicon carbide (a-SiC) on bulk LiNbO3 crystal substrate, enabling scalable, CMOS-compatible, low-cost, and high-density photonic integrated circuits without relying on thin-film LiNbO3. This integration approach breaks the long-standing cost-performance-scalability tradeoff, and intrinsically eliminates the need for sophisticated fabrication processes, including ion slicing, wafer bonding, and LiNbO3 etching. It realizes high-density, low-loss, and record high EO tuning efficiency of VpiL = 2.87 Vcm on bulk LiNbO3 crystal substrate. Furthermore, leveraging slow-light effect near photonic crystal bandgap, an 8.5-fold EO tuning efficiency enhancement is achieved, highlighting the platform's capability in confinement control and dispersion engineering.

papers.title: Information Geometry of the Geodesic Quantum $f$-Divergences
papers.abstract: We study the differential, statistical, and geometrical consequences generated by the geodesic quantum $f$-divergences introduced in [14], which are constructed by interpolating the relative modular operator and the commutant Radon-Nikodym derivative using a geodesic with parameter $t\in [0,1]$. For an invertible state $ρ$ and an operator convex function $f$, we compute the Hessian and obtain an explicit formula for the induced monotone quantum information metric $g_{ρ,t}^{(f)}$. Furthermore, we also compare these metrics with the Petz-Hasegawa metric and find the meaning of the interpolation parameter $t$ in this new geometry. We next show that the interpolation of relative modular operators $Γ_t$ in the reference purification of a state $σ$ defines a canonical finite binary experiment $(p_t,q_t)$, and introduce a log-likelihood cumulant function $Ψ_{ρ,σ}(t,s)$, recovering the Nussbaum-Szkoła distributions at $t=0$ and the Matsumoto construction at $t=1$. Finally, using Busemann functions, we endow this statistical framework with a geometric meaning in the cone of positive operators.

papers.title: Anti-Zeno boost in an autonomous quantized-piston thermal machine
papers.abstract: Anti-Zeno enhancement of quantum heat machines has been established for working fluids driven by an external classical field, but whether it can enhance extractable-work accumulation in an autonomously evolving quantized piston remains an important question. Here we study an autonomous thermal machine in which a two-level working fluid is coupled to a quantized harmonic piston and to two spectrally separated reservoirs, without external modulation. We derive a finite-time master equation for the resulting carrier and sideband channels, whose rates interpolate between the Zeno, anti-Zeno, and Markovian regimes as the coupling time is varied. For an initially coherent piston, the machine charges the piston and generates more ergotropy than the Markovian reference in the anti-Zeno window. Reversing the same retained channels turns the device into a finite-resource refrigerator with enhanced cooling. The anti-Zeno effect therefore increases the rate of operation while leaving the underlying carrier and sideband energy ratios unchanged. These channel ratios remain consistent with the usual Carnot bounds over the operating regimes considered here. Our results establish finite-time reservoir sampling as a mechanism for enhancing autonomous thermal-machine operation with a quantized piston.

papers.title: Resource-Efficient QUBO Formulation for Anchored Currency Arbitrage
papers.abstract: Currency arbitrage (CA) involves trading currencies in cycles to exploit discrepancies in market valuations. Quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) involves minimizing a quadratic cost (energy) function of binary variables. Previous works have explored the use of QUBO to solve CA problems. We build on these previous works by introducing realistic constraints such as beginning cycles from a held currency and accounting for per-transaction trading fees. We show that this formulation requires fewer logical variables (qubits) than previous QUBO encodings in the literature. We derive provably sufficient penalty weights for its constraint terms. We also introduce an exact anchor-gauge reweighting of the exchange rates that compresses the QUBO coefficient range from the rate scale to the arbitrage scale, addressing the finite analog precision of annealing hardware. We demonstrate the efficacy of this formulation using classical simulated annealing against an exact Held-Karp baseline on the same CPU and show that it can effectively find profitable cycles and account for trading fees. Finally, we benchmark faithful implementations of five prior QUBO encodings at matched sampler budgets and show that the proposed encoding is the only one to recover the exact fee-adjusted optimum.

papers.title: A certified lower bound on the quantum-capacity threshold of the depolarizing channel
papers.abstract: The noise threshold below which the qubit depolarizing channel retains positive quantum capacity has been studied since 1996. The classic constructions come with exact finite formulae, but in every reported threshold to date -- most recently the record of Agarwal et al. -- the final step, the sign of the coherent information at the reported point, is a floating-point evaluation. We give the first exact-arithmetic, independently machine-checkable positivity proofs in this regime: an explicit 45-copy rank-two input state $A$, published as a 1,472-byte witness, with certified $I_c > 0$ at the exact rational $p = 16239/250000 = 0.064956$ (per-Pauli convention; total error rate $3p = 0.194868$) -- beyond both the best value printed in the Agarwal et al. paper ($0.064657$) and the strongest state in the same authors' public repository ($\approx 0.064911$), both numerical. Because the depolarizing family is a semigroup under composition, fixed-input coherent information is nonincreasing in $p$ on $[0,1/4]$, so a single certified point extends to the entire interval below it. The same machinery confines the positivity boundaries of $A$ and of the strongest public state of Agarwal et al. to disjoint rational intervals separated by more than $1/25000$ -- to our knowledge the first proven ordering of the positivity boundaries of two explicit competing code states. Every computational claim in the paper reduces to a finite list of big-integer comparisons, checkable by a dependency-free few-hundred-line verifier whose soundness rests on three self-contained half-page lemmas. Payloads, certificates, and verifier accompany the paper as a supplementary artifact.

papers.title: Anomalous radiation pressure in strong-field ionization driven by quantum light
papers.abstract: We show that in strong-field ionization driven by bright squeezed vacuum, the mean longitudinal photoelectron momentum scales with the mean incident intensity $I$ as $I^{2/3}$, rather than linearly as under coherent-light driving. This anomalous scaling originates from a field-amplitude saddle-point structure: nonlinear tunneling selects two dominant field amplitudes of equal magnitude and opposite sign from the broad quantum fluctuations. Tracing over the final photon state erases their relative-phase information, leaving their common magnitude to determine the field-dependent longitudinal momentum shift and its $I^{2/3}$ scaling. Photon-number resolution instead preserves this coherence, producing parity-dependent modulations of the longitudinal momentum transfer through time-domain double-slit interference between two field pathways separated by half a cycle. These results establish longitudinal momentum transfer as a distinct observable in strong-field quantum optics that encodes both the photon statistics and the field coherence of intense quantum light.

papers.title: Geodesic Quantum $f$-Divergences
papers.abstract: We introduce the geodesic quantum $f$-divergences $D_f^t$, $0\leq t\leq1$, obtained from the affine-invariant geodesic between the standard and maximal relative modular operators. They reduce to the classical $f$-divergence for commuting states. The logarithmic generator yields geodesic relative entropies joining the Umegaki and Belavkin-Staszewski entropies, while the power generators yield $(t,α)$-Rényi divergences joining the Petz and geometric families. Our first main result is data processing of $D_f^t$ for every finite operator-convex generator $f$ and every $t\in[0,1]$. In particular, this gives DPI for the geodesic relative entropies and for the $(t,α)$-Rényi divergences when $0<α<1$ or $1<α\leq2$. Our second main result identifies equality in the DPI: for invertible states, every equality-determining operator-convex generator has, at each nonmaximal parameter $0\leq t<1$, exactly the Petz sufficiency class; at $t=1$, this changes to the generally larger maximal, or BS, class, which also coincides with the equality class of the divergences associated with the quadratic generator for every $t$. Our third main result is the corresponding collapse of invertible geodesic quantum Markov chains: for each of the three ordered conditional-mutual-information constructions, the $t$-quantum Markov chains are precisely the quantum Markov chains for $0\leq t<1$, whereas at $t=1$ they are the invertible BS quantum Markov chains, a class that can be strictly larger. We also determine parameter-monotonicity regimes and the intersections with the $(α,z)$ family. We prove strengthened data-processing and reconstruction estimates; we compare the three conditional orientations; we establish continuity bounds under positive lower-eigenvalue assumptions together with complementary discontinuity results; and we give a capacity-per-unit-cost interpretation.

papers.title: Topologically Protected Learning from Exceptional Point Braiding: Toward Braid Programming
papers.abstract: We present a framework for topological learning based on exceptional point (EP) braiding in a non-Hermitian Bogoliubov-de Gennes Hamiltonian. A closed algebraic equation for the EP super-surface is derived; through momentum quantisation in finite systems, it predicts the exact number and parameter positions of all EPs in real space, irrespective of system size. The EP topology is characterised by two quantised invariants the state-swap fidelity and the normalised Berry phase which cannot both be zero for a topological EP. A complete topological map shows that all EPs lie within a specefic region. Adiabatic encirclements confirm robust state swapping and yield a universal set of braid gates, including Pauli-X, Pauli-Y, Pauli-Z, a Hadamard-like gate, the T-gate, and a SWAP operation, with the special case where a is 0, providing additional phase gates. Building on these generators, we reformulate learning as braid programming a discrete search over the braid group that replaces gradient descent on continuous weights with combinatorial optimisation. A proof-of-concept genetic search successfully discovers short braid words that reproduce the standard Hadamard gate and the H.Z gate with perfect fidelity. This paradigm offers inherent noise immunity, catastrophic-forgetting prevention through compositional concatenation, and guaranteed generalisation by mathematical construction, establishing EP braiding as a promising substrate for robust, interpretable, and topologically protected neuromorphic computation.

papers.title: Resource Analysis for Quantum Simulation of Spatially Varying Transport-Reaction Equations
papers.abstract: Spatially varying coefficients are the primary source of circuit complexity in quantum simulation of linear advection-diffusion-reaction equations. This work presents a resource analysis of single-step quantum propagators constructed using sparse FABLE block encodings, Quantum Singular Value Transformation, and linear-combination-of-unitaries. We derive theoretical estimates for qubit count, gate complexity, and circuit depth in terms of the spatial discretization, sparsity, and polynomial degree, and compare these predictions with synthesized quantum circuits for one- and two-dimensional variable-coefficient problems. The resulting analysis quantifies the cost of encoding realistic transport operators and provides practical resource estimates for near-term implementations.

papers.title: Longitudinal-Field-Driven Transition in a non-integrable Non-Hermitian Transverse-Field Ising Chain via RBMs
papers.abstract: We investigate the ground-state properties and quantum critical behavior of a non-Hermitian transverse-field Ising chain subjected to longitudinal and complex transverse magnetic fields. To address this interacting many-body problem, we employ real-valued neural quantum states based on Restricted Boltzmann Machines (RBMs), optimized using Variational Monte Carlo (VMC) sampling. Spectral analysis of finite chains reveals exceptional points associated with spontaneous parity-time (PT) symmetry breaking. A real-valued RBM framework is developed to reconstruct the ground-state eigenstates of the non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. Benchmark comparisons with exact diagonalization demonstrate that the RBM approach accurately reproduces the ground-state energy, magnetization, and spin-spin correlations. Extending the analysis to larger system sizes, we identify a non-Hermitian quantum phase transition characterized by PT-symmetry breaking and the emergence of magnetic order. Our results establish real-valued neural quantum states as an efficient and scalable framework for investigating critical phenomena in interacting non-Hermitian quantum systems.

papers.title: Experimental High-Dimensional Quantum Overlapping Tomography
papers.abstract: Large-scale quantum systems have advanced rapidly via the exploration of more particles and higher dimensions, offering great potential for developing quantum technologies. However, their characterization becomes prohibitive with increasing local dimensionality and particle number. Here we propose high-dimensional quantum overlapping tomography based on a graph-theoretic formulation, which allows one to efficiently reconstruct few-body marginals of multipartite high-dimensional quantum systems. We experimentally realize it on a photonic four-party entangled state in a $4 \times 4 \times 2 \times 2$ system. Using measurements in mutually unbiased bases, we reconstruct all six two-body marginals with only 25 projective measurement settings, compared with 94 and 225 settings for independent tomography of all two-body reduced states and full state tomography, respectively. The reconstructed marginals reveal a layered entanglement structure vital for high-dimensional quantum networks. We further show that these marginals enable more noise-resilient certification of multipartite high-dimensional entanglement than the fidelity-based criterion. Our work thus offers a scalable route for learning multidimensional quantum systems.

papers.title: Machine Learning Approaches to Decoding Topological Quantum Codes
papers.abstract: Decoding is an essential component of quantum error correction (QEC), translating stabilizer measurement outcomes into corrective actions that suppress logical errors and preserve logical quantum information. Building fault-tolerant architectures requires increasing the code distance, which in turn places growing demands on decoding accuracy, scalability, and practical deployability. While a wide range of decoding algorithms have been proposed and demonstrated, achieving reliable, scalable, and real-time decoding remains a significant challenge. Machine-learning (ML) approaches are particularly well suited to this setting, as quantum error decoding is fundamentally a problem of processing large volumes of classical data with complex spatiotemporal correlations. This chapter surveys ML-based methods for quantum error decoding, with a focus on topological codes and an emphasis on architectural principles, practical performance, and real-time considerations. We first frame decoding as a learning problem and outline key paradigms, including discriminative, generative, and reinforcement-learning formulations. We then introduce the neural network building blocks that underpin most contemporary neural decoders and discuss how these components can be integrated to balance expressivity, scalability, and latency. Building on this architectural perspective, we review recent progress and benchmarks in neural decoding for memory experiments, and discuss real-time decoding, open challenges, and future directions toward scalable fault-tolerant quantum computing.

papers.title: Renormalization Group Analysis of Pairing Instabilities in Nuclear Fermi Liquids
papers.abstract: A nuclear Fermi liquid exhibits competing pairing instabilities in different spin, isospin, and orbital channels. In a Fermi-surface renormalization group (RG) treatment, the channel that develops a pole first is determined not only by its tree-level attraction but also by its one-loop RG coefficient. We illustrate this mechanism in a minimal $S/P$-wave model. A spherical Fermi surface establishes the reference competition between the lowest even- and odd-parity interactions. Axial deformation changes the relevant Fermi-surface integrals and lifts the degeneracy between longitudinal and transverse $P$-wave components. In isospin-asymmetric matter, neutron--proton Fermi-momentum splitting restricts the simultaneous low-energy contribution of the two species and can terminate the $np$ running at finite threshold scales. Our calculations are intended as controlled one-loop RG illustrations rather than as quantitative nuclear-matter calculations. We show how the Fermi-surface geometry and composition can change the ordering of competing pairing instabilities.

papers.title: Designing Quantum Error Correcting Codes to fit decoders via Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: We present a reinforcement learning (RL) approach to the co-design of stabilizer sets of Quantum Error Correcting Codes (QECCs) and decoders. We show how to produce a generative model that produces Bivariate Bicycle (BB) codes based on the choice of decoder. Specifically, we fix a decoder architecture and use Proximal Policy Optimisation (PPO) to train an agent over BB codes to maximise decoder performance under a depolarising channel noise model.

papers.title: Tunable Statistics-Induced Caging in the Anyon-Hubbard Model
papers.abstract: We study the quantum dynamics of two interacting anyons in the Anyon-Hubbard model on a four-site plaquette, a system that is exactly mappable to a Bose-Hubbard model. We reveal that static Aharonov-Bohm (AB) caging, induced by only specific statistical phases, emerges in the strongly interacting limit but breaks down under weak interparticle interactions. To address this, we demonstrate that statistical-factor-induced AB caging can be dynamically restored via Floquet engineering. This dynamical mechanism, governed by the synthetic Floquet flux and the anyonic statistical phase, extends the caging effect into the weakly interacting regime across the full spectrum of statistical phases. Furthermore, we show that the external drive enables the selective caging of anyons, providing an efficient approach for manipulating anyons and identifying statistical phases.

papers.title: Benign Projective Landscapes for Measured Quantum Divergences
papers.abstract: We study nonconvex optimization of measured quantum $f$-divergences over rank-one projective measurements. For smoothly operator-Fenchel liftable generators and faithful states, every projective local maximum and every second-order stationary point is globally optimal over all POVMs. The criterion is blockwise: a critical PVM is optimal exactly when the compressed states are proportional on each equal-score block; otherwise an explicit two-vector rotation has positive ascent curvature. Operator-convex generators admit a positive atomic curvature resolution, and the quadratic $χ^2$ case yields two-sided residual bounds. For binary accessible information, this framework proves the known adaptive-capacity equality and shows that every nonidentical qubit ensemble has exactly two stationary projective measurements, proving conjectures of Keil and Thai--Dall'Arno. A rare-prior limit connects weighted Jensen--Shannon information to relative entropy and yields a finite counterexample to the proposed equivalence between observational-entropy and all-ensemble mutual-information orders. The landscape theorem also covers measured Rényi divergences of finite positive order and measured relative entropy.

papers.title: Quantum Kernel k-Means for Credit-Card Fraud Detection:A Controlled Benchmark on Real Transaction Data
papers.abstract: We benchmarked quantum kernel $k$-means against classical clustering for credit-card fraud detection on real transaction data, at up to \MaxQubits{} qubits, under a protocol with separated selection and reporting data and matched search budgets. We find no robust quantum advantage: the sign of the difference depends on register size, all effect sizes are below $0.013$ ARI, and the single significant advantage we observe is fully explained by the number of configurations searched. We further show that ordinary hyperparameter choices move performance by considerably more than the quantum kernel does, that additional qubits degrade rather than improve performance through kernel concentration, and that the clustering framing itself fails at realistic class imbalance though kernel-based anomaly scoring does not. We regard the methodological contribution as the more durable one. The search-budget ablation in particular is inexpensive and, in our case, decisive: it converted a statistically significant advantage into a procedural artefact. We would encourage its routine use.

papers.title: Continuous Quantum Feedback Control via Kraus-Parameterized Belief Reinforcement Learning
papers.abstract: Quantum feedback control requires acting on noisy continuous measurement records without direct access to the underlying quantum state. We propose Kraus-Parameterized Belief Reinforcement Learning, a pipeline in which a recurrent encoder, constrained to the Stiefel manifold, produces density-matrix estimates that are guaranteed positive-semidefinite and trace-normalized by construction, embedding quantum state geometry directly into the learning loop. A Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) actor then maps these physically valid belief states to continuous control actions. On a simulated continuously monitored qubit, the resulting policy achieves stable feedback control, maintaining a measurement-conditioned belief fidelity of approximately 0.77-0.80 and exhibiting substantially lower return variance than a parameter-matched LSTM-history baseline across both nominal and out-of-distribution conditions. Although gains in raw target fidelity are modest, the geometric constraint guarantees a physically valid, interpretable belief representation and yields markedly more stable control under measurement inefficiency and abrupt dynamics switches. These results indicate that physics-informed neural memory is a practical inductive bias for reliable quantum feedback control.

papers.title: Rand-SEMI-QAOA: Finite-Budget Depth-One MaxCut Ensembles on Compressed Quantum Registers
papers.abstract: We introduce Rand-SEMI-QAOA, a finite-budget QRAO--QAOA ensemble for MaxCut based on a $(3,1)$-QRAC relaxation. The method samples labels uniformly without replacement from the product-$X$ family of an implemented Galois stabilizer mutually unbiased basis (MUB) system. Each selected state--mixer pair is optimized independently for relaxed QRAO energy and then evaluated by deterministic Pauli-sign decoding. Exhaustive scans of the implemented noncomputational MUB catalog place the product-$X$ family first in 18 of 20 validated family-mean cells and in every tested cell for $r=5,6,7$. On a complete cohort of $2{,}400$ random connected 3-regular MaxCut instances with $n\in\{18,20,22\}$, the capped matched-cardinality schedule attains a graph-mean decoded best-of-set approximation ratio of $0.9421$ with one QAOA layer, while the $K=r^2$ schedule attains $0.9319$. These statistics are conditional on the disclosed frozen selector pools and do not estimate variability over selector seeds. An exact gauge identity shows that product-family labels generate the orbit of the QRAO Hamiltonian under an $r$-dimensional sign-gauge group. For common angles and relaxed energy, deterministic syndrome analysis proves branchwise dephasing, while an anisotropic Gaussian surrogate controls the coherent label-averaged response on the scale $β=b/r$. The theory does not order independently optimized decoded maxima. The results are finite-size and resource-explicit and do not establish quantum advantage.

papers.title: Charging of a Quantum Battery by a Two-Photon Quantum Pulse
papers.abstract: We investigate the charging of a harmonic-oscillator quantum battery by a propagating two-photon quantum pulse coupled through a two-level-system charger. Excitation-number conservation reduces the dynamics to a sequential response of the first and second excitation sectors, whose effective non-Hermitian generators exhibit two exceptional points separating overdamped, mixed, and underdamped regimes. We derive the exact full-charging amplitude and the response-matched two-photon temporal mode that achieves perfect charging in the ideal resonant single-channel model. For experimentally accessible Gaussian pulses, moderate temporal anticorrelation or a finite photon delay can enhance charging, whereas positive correlations generally suppress it. States with equal Schmidt number can nevertheless show different charging efficiencies, demonstrating that temporal-mode structure and response matching, rather than nonseparability alone, determine charging performance.

papers.title: A scalable chip-integrated single-photon source array based on 50 individually addressable neutral atoms
papers.abstract: Scalable arrays of identical single-photon sources are a central resource for photonic quantum information processing, quantum networks and quantum metrology. Neutral atoms provide intrinsically identical emitters that can be assembled and rearranged in optical tweezers, but a many-channel fiber interface to individually trapped atoms has remained a major technical challenge. Here we demonstrate a chip-interfaced single-photon source array based on 50 individually addressable $^{87}\mathrm{Rb}$ atoms. A glass waveguide fan-out converts the \SI{5}{\micro m} pitch of the optical-tweezer array to the \SI{127}{\micro m} pitch of a commercial fiber array, mapping each atom to its own waveguide, fiber and single-photon detector. We resolve all 50 channels with an average nearest-neighbor cross-talk of $0.4\%$ and a uniform insertion loss of \SI{2.9}{dB}, and verify single-photon emission with $g^{(2)}(0)=0.29$, presently limited by detector dark counts and residual cooling-light scattering. Combining per-channel atom discrimination, rearrangement and reservoir replenishment, we prepare source subarrays of up to 24 atoms with a $93\%$ fill fraction. For small target numbers, atom loss is repaired from the reservoir at the detection-limited rate of \SI{118}{Hz}. We further fabricate a 784-channel waveguide chip, showing that the photonic interface can be extended well beyond the present number. This architecture establishes a fiber-native neutral-atom platform for larger arrays of identical single-photon sources.

papers.title: Finite-energy GKP-QPC architectures for photonic quantum memories and repeaters
papers.abstract: Photonic quantum networks require error-correction architectures that remain useful with finite-energy bosonic states, pure-loss fiber transmission, and explicit resource accounting. In this light, we study a concatenated architecture in which each physical rail is a finitely squeezed Gottesman--Kitaev--Preskill (GKP) qubit transmitted through a pure-loss fiber segment, corrected by teleportation-based GKP error correction with finitely squeezed ancillae, and decoded by an outer quantum parity code (QPC). The GKP layer converts continuous homodyne syndromes into effective rail-level Pauli marginals, while the QPC layer suppresses the residual qubit-level errors. For the concatenated code family considered here, we find a finite-squeezing threshold of $5.06\,\mathrm{dB}$ at zero propagation loss. In the memory setting, the QPC layer lowers the squeezing at which repeated error correction becomes beneficial from $6.7\,\mathrm{dB}$ for bare GKP correction to $5.2\,\mathrm{dB}$ for QPC$(3,3)$ and $4.3\,\mathrm{dB}$ for QPC$(5,5)$, and improves the average-fidelity ratio by up to $75$--$90\%$ in the relevant intermediate-noise regime. In the repeater setting, avoiding pre-amplification gives larger secret-key fractions at moderate squeezing, but also produces an optimal squeezing because highly squeezed GKP peaks become sensitive to loss-induced inward displacement. Resource-normalized rates show that QPC concatenation can exceed the repeaterless PLOB benchmark by orders of magnitude and extend the communication reach, at short repeater spacing, to distances of order $10^4$km with $14$dB squeezing. However, QPC concatenation becomes detrimental when each elementary hop is too lossy. These results provide quantitative design rules for finite-squeezing GKP--QPC quantum memories and repeaters.

papers.title: Benchmarking Quantum Machine Learning for Power-System Attack Detection: Evaluation Choices Decide the Outcome Before the Models Do
papers.abstract: Machine-learning detectors for power-system cyberattacks are themselves attack surfaces, and quantum machine learning has been proposed for them. We benchmark fidelity-kernel SVMs and variational classifiers against six tuned classical models on public power-system attack data (Mississippi State/ORNL), across white-box, transfer, decision-based black-box, and poisoning attacks. Our headline finding is methodological: the benchmark's answers are set by the evaluator's choices before the models. Eight choices -- six in the evaluation protocol, two in the tuning the benchmark itself runs -- each reversed or moved a conclusion at fixed models. The largest is the split: the row-level protocol scores 0.905 macro-F1 where holding whole source files out leaves 0.594, and in the capped matched-dimensionality regime the quantum arm sits within noise of chance with the classical arm 0.024 above it. A fidelity kernel looks most robust until attacked directly (retention 0.886 to 0.064); a mis-fitted surrogate manufactures a 10x asymmetry; an unseeded black-box attack moves 75% between restarts. A positive control explains the accuracy null: the labels, not the pipeline. We give the control that catches each choice and release the seeded benchmark.

papers.title: Linear optical fan-out gates using fewer ancillary single photons with enhanced success probability
papers.abstract: Photonic quantum gates are fundamental building blocks for a wide range of optical quantum information processing tasks. We propose an efficient linear-optical scheme for implementing a post-selected three-qubit fan-out gate (also known as a controlled-NOT-NOT gate) using only two ancillary single photons and linear optical elements. The scheme can be generalized to an $n$-qubit fan-out gate, requiring $(n-1)$ ancillary single photons and $(3n-3)$ polarizing beam splitters (PBSs), with a success probability of $\left(\frac{1}{4}\right)^{n-1}$. Compared to the standard gate decomposition approach, which requires $(2n-2)$ ancillary single photons, $(5n-5)$ PBSs, and yields a success probability of $\left(\frac{1}{8}\right)^{n-1}$. Our scheme significantly reduces the resource overhead and improves the success probability. We further evaluate the gate performance and demonstrate improved robustness compared to gate decomposition-based methods.

papers.title: Position-dependent thermalization of two-level probes in de Sitter spacetime: Interplay between Gibbons-Hawking and Unruh effects
papers.abstract: We investigate the thermalization process of two-level probes in de Sitter spacetime from a quantum-metrological perspective. For a static probe separated by a finite distance from a freely falling observer, both the intrinsic Gibbons--Hawking temperature and the position-dependent Unruh temperature are encoded in the probe state. The mutual influence between the encoding rate of the Gibbons--Hawking temperature and that of the Unruh temperature is studied. Results show that the thermalization rate is equal to the sum of the encoding rates of the Gibbons--Hawking temperature and that of the Unruh temperature. Interestingly, a nonzero inherent acceleration induced by the separation between the probe and a freely falling observer does not necessarily suppress the encoding of the Gibbons--Hawking temperature. Instead, there exists an optimal inherent acceleration at which the encoding rate of the Gibbons--Hawking temperature is maximized. Furthermore, the required total probe time of estimating the thermal effect with sufficient precision is shown in relation with the thermalization rate. The required total probe time and the corresponding number of probes remain experimentally feasible when the position-dependent inherent acceleration satisfies $\frac{a}{2πω_0}\rightarrow0.1$.

papers.title: Nonlinear Landau-Zener Tunneling with Heat-Bath Colored Noise
papers.abstract: In this work, we investigate the influence of colored noise originating from a heat bath on nonlinear Landau-Zener (LZ) tunneling. The nonlinearity might arise intrinsically from many-body mean-field atomic self-interactions or Kerr nonlinearities in optical systems.
